Honestly, for someone who dances with the devil, the setting is pretty fitting.

On Wednesday's episode of The Daily Show, host Josh Johnson pointed out one detail of Donald Trump Jr.'s wedding that looks like it pulled in a wildly popular horror movie — and once you see it, you can't unsee it.

Johnson first aired footage Trump shared on social media of his wedding to socialite Bettina Trump, which was held in May on a small island in the Bahamas, then dropped this brutal line.

The clip was set to an acoustic version of The Ronettes classic "Be My Baby," opening with an aerial shot of the church where the president's eldest son wed, then showing interior shots of guests inside. The footage shows Trump Jr.'s sisters — Ivanka and Tiffany Trump — seated in a pew, before cutting to slow motion of the bride and groom embracing at the altar, a giant cross suspended above them.

"Truly a beautiful wedding ceremony… in the church from Sinners," Johnson joked, with a still from the Oscar-winning film shown beside him, depicting Sammie (played by Miles Caton) walking into his father's blood-splattered church. Above Sammie — just like above Don Jr. and his bride — hangs a giant cross. The exterior of the church in Sinners also bears a striking resemblance to the church in the Bahamas.

Donald Trump Jr.'s wedding has recently drawn controversy because ProPublica reported earlier that the wedding was fully paid for by Russian oligarch Umar Kremlev, who has close ties to Russian President Vladimir Putin.

In response to the furore, Bettina Trump issued a statement on Instagram clarifying: "Don and I got married privately on Friday with just our family."

She continued: "The following weekend was planned long ago — it was a weekend with friends. It was not our wedding weekend. Our original wedding plans changed, and we simply decided to get married earlier and show up to an already-planned weekend as a newly married couple."

She also wrote that the couple's "good friend Umar generously threw us two incredible celebration nights after we got married."

Johnson also had a pretty cutting response to Bettina Trump's clarification.

"Yes, exactly, fake news," Johnson said, impersonating Bettina Trump. "They didn't pay for my wedding, they paid for a more expensive after-party."
